objectives: Catalog astronomical transients + their physical mechanisms.
Reason about pulsars, magnetars, FRBs, and tests of GR.

slides.title: Transients: supernovae, GRBs, TDEs, kilonovae
slides.body:
**Time-domain astronomy** = systematic study of variable + transient sources. The sky is not static — every night thousands of objects brighten + fade across the EM spectrum. Modern surveys (ZTF, ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, ASAS-SN, Gaia, Vera Rubin LSST) generate ~10⁶ alerts per night.

**Supernovae (SNe)**: stellar explosions. Decades of classification + physical understanding:
- **Type Ia**: thermonuclear runaway of CO white dwarf crossing Chandrasekhar limit via accretion (single-degenerate) or merger (double-degenerate). Total disruption. Light-curve standardizable → cosmological distance ladder. **Perlmutter, Schmidt, Riess 1998-99** → accelerating universe → dark energy → 2011 Nobel.
- **Type II**: core-collapse of massive star (M > 8 M☉) with H envelope. **SN1987A** (LMC, closest modern Type II): neutrinos detected by Kamiokande + IMB + Baksan ~3 hr before optical brightening — confirmed core-collapse model + neutrino burst expectation.
- **Type Ib/c**: core-collapse without H envelope (Ib has He; Ic lacks both — stripped-envelope progenitors via winds or binary mass transfer). Often associated with long GRBs.
- **Superluminous SNe (SLSN)**: 10-100× brighter than Type Ia; magnetar-driven or pair-instability candidates.
- **Pair-instability SNe**: very massive stars (140-260 M☉); γ-ray photon-photon → e⁻e⁺ pair production removes core pressure support → total disruption, no remnant.

**Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs)**:
- **Discovered by Klebesadel + Strong + Olson 1973** (Vela nuclear-test detection satellites, paper appeared after Cold War declassification). Brief (~ms-100s) γ-ray flashes from random sky directions.
- **Bimodal duration distribution**:
  - **Long GRBs** (>2 s): collapsar — massive-star core collapse to BH with rotating accretion disk + relativistic jet. Often associated with broad-line Type Ic SNe.
  - **Short GRBs** (<2 s): compact-object mergers (NS-NS, NS-BH). Confirmed by GW170817.
- Beaming → jet opening angle ~5° → true rate ~500-1000× observed; correction factor.
- Afterglow in X-ray + optical + radio over hours-days-weeks → shock physics + circumburst medium.
- BAT/Swift + Fermi-GBM monitor in real-time; ground follow-up worldwide.

**Tidal disruption events (TDEs)**: a star wandering too close to a SMBH is torn apart by tidal forces; ~half mass accretes → bright multi-wavelength flare lasting months-years. Rees 1988 predicted; ASASSN-14li + AT2019qiz are well-studied examples. Light-echo + spectral evolution probe BH accretion physics.

**Kilonovae**: optical/IR transients from NS-NS or NS-BH mergers, powered by **r-process radioactive decay** of newly synthesized heavy elements. Predicted Li-Paczyński 1998. **GW170817 / AT2017gfo** (Aug 17, 2017) — first confirmed kilonova; spectroscopic detection of Sr (Watson 2019) + Pian + Tanvir + Smartt + Drout discovery papers — direct evidence of r-process site for Au, Pt, lanthanides.

**Other transients**: novae (white-dwarf surface H-burning bursts), variable stars (Cepheids, RR Lyrae, Miras), cataclysmic variables (CV — accreting WD binaries), microlensing events (OGLE detection rate ~1000/yr), stellar flares (M-dwarf superflares), Earth-impacting bolides + meteors. Each contains different physics.

slides.title: Gravitational waves + multimessenger astronomy
slides.body:
**Predicted by Einstein 1916** as ripples in spacetime curvature radiated by accelerating masses: h ~ (G/c⁴) × Q̈ ~ 10⁻²¹ for solar-mass binaries at typical extragalactic distances — far below the noise of any conceivable detector for decades.

**Hulse + Taylor 1974**: discovered the **binary pulsar PSR B1913+16** — two NSs in 7.75-hr orbit. Decades of pulse timing revealed orbital decay matching GR's GW-radiation prediction to <1%. Indirect proof of GW. **Nobel 1993** (Hulse + Taylor).

**LIGO direct detection**:
- **Laser Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory**: 4-km Michelson interferometers at Hanford WA + Livingston LA. Sensitivity ~10⁻¹⁸ m (subnuclear) over 4-km arms.
- **GW150914** (14 Sept 2015): first direct detection — 30 M☉ + 35 M☉ BHs merging at z = 0.09; signal duration 0.2 s; mass loss → 3 M☉ × c² of GW energy radiated in <1 s (peak GW luminosity 200 M☉c²/s — exceeded total EM luminosity of observable universe briefly).
- **Weiss + Barish + Thorne Nobel 2017**.
- **O3 + O4 runs** (2019-2024): >200 BBH detections; chirp-mass + spin + inclination distributions constrain stellar-evolution + binary formation channels.

**Virgo** (Italy/France) + **KAGRA** (Japan) joined LIGO → 3+ detector network → sky localization to ~degrees.

**GW170817** (Aug 17, 2017): **first NS-NS merger detection** — multimessenger watershed:
- LIGO/Virgo: 100-s inspiral chirp; localized to 28 sq deg.
- Fermi-GBM: short GRB GRB170817A detected 1.7 s after merger.
- Optical/IR (DECam + Swope + Las Cumbres Observatory + many more, within 11 hr): kilonova **AT2017gfo** identified in NGC 4993 (~40 Mpc).
- Days-weeks: UV/optical/IR kilonova SED evolution; r-process Sr/Te/Au/Pt/lanthanide spectroscopic signatures.
- Radio + X-ray afterglow over months-years (Chandra, VLA, JVLA): jet structure.
- **Confirmations**:
  - r-process nucleosynthesis site = compact-object mergers (B²FH 1957 unresolved question).
  - Speed of gravity = speed of light to 1 part in 10¹⁵ (1.7 s delay over 40 Mpc).
  - NS equation of state constraints (deformability parameter Λ).
  - First standard-siren H₀ measurement (~70 km/s/Mpc).

**Black-hole + neutron-star merger populations** (O1-O4):
- BBH masses range from 5-150 M☉; many > 30 M☉ BHs not seen electromagnetically.
- GW190521: most massive BBH; possible pair-instability gap progenitor.
- GW200115 + GW200105: first NS-BH mergers.
- Mass distribution + spin distribution constrain binary evolution channels (isolated binary vs dynamical formation in clusters).

**Future GW**:
- **LISA** (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, 2034 launch): 2.5-Mkm triangular constellation at L1; mHz GW band — SMBH-SMBH mergers, EMRIs (extreme mass-ratio inspirals), galactic binaries, possible stochastic backgrounds. Bridges to PTA + LIGO bands.
- **Cosmic Explorer + Einstein Telescope** (~2035): 40-km + underground 10-km arms; ground 3rd-gen sensitivity 10× better; deep population statistics.
- **PTA (Pulsar Timing Arrays)**: NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, MeerKAT + IPTA — nanohertz GW band (yrs-period waves); 2023 announced detection of stochastic background, likely SMBH binaries at galactic centers.
- **NEMO**, **TianQin**, **DECIGO**: future concepts.

**Multi-messenger astronomy (MMA)** = combining EM + GW + neutrinos + cosmic rays. IceCube TXS 0506+056 (2017): high-energy neutrino correlated with flaring blazar (~3σ). **Multi-messenger transient alerts** (GCN, LIGO alerts, ZTF, Rubin LSST) coordinate global follow-up infrastructure.

slides.title: Pulsars, magnetars, FRBs + tests of GR
slides.body:
**Pulsars**: rapidly rotating **neutron stars** with strong magnetic fields, emitting beams of radio (+ optical, X-ray, γ-ray) along their magnetic poles. As the beam sweeps past Earth, we see periodic pulses — like a lighthouse.
- **Discovered Jocelyn Bell + Antony Hewish 1967** (Cambridge): noticed periodic radio signal LGM-1 ('Little Green Men' initially — quickly identified as natural). PSR B1919+21 first pulsar. **Hewish + Ryle Nobel 1974** (Bell controversially excluded — Matthew effect; Bell got posthumous Breakthrough Prize 2018).
- ~3300 known pulsars (ATNF catalog 2024). Periods 1.4 ms (millisecond pulsars, spun up by binary accretion) to ~10 s.
- **Magnetic field** ~10⁸-10¹² G; spin energy lost via magnetic dipole radiation + relativistic wind.
- **Crab pulsar** (PSR B0531+21, in Crab Nebula from SN 1054 historical Chinese record): canonical young pulsar, 33 ms period, visible-light pulsations.

**Magnetars**: extreme-magnetic-field NSs (B ~10¹⁴-10¹⁵ G; Duncan + Thompson 1992). Soft gamma repeaters (SGRs) + anomalous X-ray pulsars (AXPs). Magnetic-field decay powers giant flares (e.g., SGR 1806-20 giant flare 2004 — briefly outshone whole galaxy in γ-rays).

**Fast radio bursts (FRBs)**:
- **Lorimer 2007**: discovered Lorimer burst in archival Parkes data — millisecond-duration radio flash with dispersion measure (DM) far exceeding galactic value → extragalactic. First FRB.
- ~1000 FRBs known (CHIME-FRB catalog 2021); 50+ repeaters (most famous **FRB121102**, **FRB180916**).
- Mostly one-shot but some repeat → multiple emission mechanisms likely.
- **Origin**: 2020 — **SGR 1935+2154** (galactic magnetar) emitted FRB-like burst → magnetars are at least one FRB source. Many other models survive: NS-NS collision, BH-NS, supranova, primordial-BH evaporation, alien tech (Loeb speculation).
- **CHIME-FRB** (Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment): wide-field FRB hunter, ~hundreds/yr detections.
- **Future**: SKA, DSA-2000, BURSTT — characterize host galaxies + propagation effects + cosmography (DM-z relation as 'missing baryon' probe).

**Cataclysmic variables (CV)**: accreting WD binaries with Roche-lobe overflow → outbursts (novae, dwarf novae); polars + intermediate polars depending on B-field; Type Ia progenitor candidates.

**Microlensing as time-domain**:
- **OGLE** (Optical Gravitational Lensing Experiment, Warsaw, 1992-): monitors millions of stars in Galactic bulge + Magellanic Clouds; detected thousands of microlensing events (dark-matter compact objects + exoplanets).
- Microlensing-discovered exoplanets: especially **cold + low-mass + free-floating planets** unreachable by RV or transit.
- **Vera Rubin LSST** (2025 first light): will add microlensing surveys at unprecedented depth.

**Exoplanet transits as time-domain**: Kepler, TESS, PLATO transit surveys (treated in planetary lesson).

**Tests of GR in strong-field regime**:
- **Pulsar timing**: PSR B1913+16 (Hulse-Taylor) + PSR J0737-3039 (double pulsar) — best confirmations of GW radiation reaction, geodetic precession, Shapiro delay. Tests of GR alternatives (scalar-tensor theories) at 10⁻⁵ level.
- **GW150914+**: BBH ringdown matches Kerr predictions; bound parameterized post-Newtonian (PPN) deviations.
- **Sgr A* S-star orbits + EHT image**: GR tests at horizon scale.
- **Clifford Will + Frans Pretorius** + others: theoretical/numerical relativity infrastructure underpinning these tests. Will's *Theory and Experiment in Gravitational Physics* (1981, 2018 2nd ed.) is the canonical reference.

**Vera Rubin Observatory + LSST (2025 first light)**:
- 8.4 m Simonyi Survey Telescope at Cerro Pachón, Chile.
- 9.6 sq deg field of view, 3.2 Gpix camera, 30-s exposures.
- Survey ~half the sky every 3-4 nights for 10 yr.
- Expected: ~10⁷ transient alerts per year (SNe, NEAs, microlensing, AGN variability, kilonovae, TDEs).
- Real-time alert broker network: **Lasair**, **ALeRCE**, **AMPEL**, **Antares**, **Pitt-Google** — distribute + classify + prioritize.
- ML classification + anomaly detection at industrial scale.

Time-domain + multimessenger is the **frontier of 2020s + 2030s astronomy** — most of what we see is variable, transient, and tells us about the most extreme physics in the universe.

question.question: Estimate GW strain from a stellar BBH at 100 Mpc
question.goal: Use order-of-magnitude GW formula to predict strain amplitude h for a 30+30 M☉ binary merger at 100 Mpc + compare to LIGO sensitivity 10⁻²¹.

steps.prompt: Use h ~ (G/c⁴) × (Mv²)/r for orbital quadrupole. Estimate Mv² near merger (v ~ c/3, M = 60 M☉, r = 100 Mpc).

acceptedAnswers: Mv² ≈ 60 M☉ × (c/3)² ≈ 60 × 2×10³⁰ kg × 10¹⁶ m²/s² ≈ 1.2×10⁴⁸ J (kinetic energy near merger)

steps.reveal: Near merger orbital kinetic energy ~ Mc²/few. Mv² ≈ 60 M☉ × c²/10 ≈ 60 × 2×10³⁰ × 9×10¹⁶ / 10 ≈ 10⁴⁸ J. About 5% of total rest-mass energy of merging BHs.

steps.prompt: Compute G/c⁴ + multiply by Mv²/r with r = 100 Mpc ≈ 3×10²⁴ m.
steps.reveal: G/c⁴ ≈ 8.26×10⁻⁴⁵ m/J. h ~ G/c⁴ × Mv²/r ~ 8.26×10⁻⁴⁵ × 10⁴⁸ / 3×10²⁴ ≈ 10⁻²¹. Matches LIGO observed strain for GW150914-like events (10⁻²¹) at ~100 Mpc luminosity distance. The order-of-magnitude works.

steps.prompt: What displacement does h = 10⁻²¹ produce in a 4-km LIGO arm?
steps.reveal: ΔL = h × L ~ 10⁻²¹ × 4×10³ m = 4×10⁻¹⁸ m. That's ~10⁻³ of a proton radius — and LIGO measures this routinely. The technological achievement is staggering: precision interferometry at <10⁻¹⁸ m across 4 km, isolated from thousands of seismic + thermal + photon-shot sources.

steps.prompt: How does h scale with distance? With chirp mass?

acceptedAnswers: h ~ M^(5/3) ω^(2/3) / r in inspiral — linear inverse distance, steep mass dependence via chirp mass M_c = (m₁m₂)^(3/5)/(m₁+m₂)^(1/5)

steps.reveal: Inspiral: h ~ G^(5/3) c^(-4) ω^(2/3) M_c^(5/3) / d_L — linear in inverse distance (1/r) + steep in chirp mass M_c. So GW detector volume scales as h^(-3) → distance reach × 2 = 8× volume → 8× event rate for same sensitivity. Next-gen detectors (Cosmic Explorer, Einstein Telescope) 10× sensitivity → 1000× detection rate.

question.question: Why did GW170817 transform astrophysics in a single event?
options: GW170817 (Aug 17, 2017) was the **first multimessenger detection of a NS-NS merger**: LIGO+Virgo GW signal localized to 28 sq deg; Fermi-GBM detected short GRB 170817A 1.7 s later; optical/IR kilonova AT2017gfo identified in NGC 4993 ~11 hr later via DECam/Swope/LCO. Single event yielded: (1) confirmation that NS-NS mergers produce short GRBs; (2) direct evidence of r-process nucleosynthesis from spectroscopic Sr/lanthanide signatures — solving the B²FH 1957 question; (3) speed of gravity = speed of light to 10⁻¹⁵; (4) NS equation-of-state constraints from tidal deformability; (5) first standard-siren H₀ measurement. Single event accomplished what whole sub-fields had pursued for decades. The dawn of multi-messenger astronomy.
question.explanation: GW170817 was an unprecedented multimessenger event delivering 5+ landmark results in one merger: (1) NS-NS produces short GRB confirmed (Klebesadel 1973 → 2017 resolution); (2) r-process site = NS-NS mergers via kilonova spectroscopy (Au, Pt, lanthanides — B²FH 1957 puzzle); (3) c_GW = c to <10⁻¹⁵; (4) NS EOS via tidal Λ; (5) standard-siren H₀. Single event = multiple Nobels-worth of physics. Multimessenger astronomy = new era.

hints: What separate questions did one event resolve?
slides.workedSolution: GW170817: GW + short GRB + kilonova + afterglow over months — confirmed NS-NS as short-GRB progenitors + r-process site (B²FH solved), measured c_GW = c (10⁻¹⁵), constrained NS EOS, gave first standard-siren H₀. Single event ≈ several Nobel-quality results. Birth of multi-messenger era.

question.question: Vera Rubin LSST (2025 first light) will issue ~10⁷ transient alerts per year. Most are routine variable stars + asteroids. Some are once-in-a-decade discoveries.
question.prompt: Walk through the data + decision pipeline: (1) photometric difference imaging detects flux change in image subtraction; (2) alert is broadcast via VOEvent + Kafka in <60 s with sky position + magnitude + color; (3) broker networks (Lasair, ALeRCE, Antares, AMPEL, Pitt-Google) classify candidates using ML (random forest, deep learning — Charnock + Moss 2017 ConvNets, Stein anomaly detection); (4) prioritization for telescope-time follow-up; (5) coordination of multi-band photometry + spectroscopy via existing networks (ePESSTO+, MOSFIT, ELT, Keck); (6) GW170817-style cases require global hours-of-notice response. What systems break under 10⁷ alerts/yr? How does ML scale + what are open problems (label imbalance, novelty detection, false positives)?

question.question: Write the gravitational-wave amplitude (strain) of LIGO's first detection GW150914 at peak.
question.hint: Order of magnitude detected by LIGO at ~410 Mpc luminosity distance.

slides.workedSolution: Peak strain h ≈ 10⁻²¹ for GW150914 at ~410 Mpc. Equivalent to ΔL/L = 10⁻²¹ in 4-km LIGO arms = 4×10⁻¹⁸ m displacement (~10⁻³ of proton radius). Detected by Hanford + Livingston interferometers 7 ms apart; identified as 36+29 M☉ BBH merger at z=0.09 in <1 day. Weiss + Barish + Thorne Nobel 2017.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why time-domain + multimessenger astronomy is the dominant frontier of the 2020s-2030s.
question.rubric: Mentions: (1) Most extreme physics + most discoveries come from transients — SNe, GRBs (Klebesadel 1973), TDEs, kilonovae, FRBs (Lorimer 2007), GW events. Pulsars + magnetars + binary-pulsar GR tests (Hulse-Taylor Nobel 1993; Will + Pretorius theory). (2) GW + EM + ν + cosmic rays combined = multimessenger astronomy (MMA) — gives total picture of most extreme events. (3) GW170817 (Aug 2017) — first MMA + kilonova + short-GRB confirmation + r-process site (B²FH 1957) + c_GW = c + standard-siren H₀. (4) Surveys generate huge alert streams: ZTF, ATLAS, Pan-STARRS, ASAS-SN, Gaia, Vera Rubin LSST (~10⁷/yr from 2025). (5) ML alert classification + global coordination (broker networks, GCN). (6) LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA + future LISA (2034) + Cosmic Explorer/ET (2035) expand discovery space. (7) Time-domain reveals fastest + most violent + most distant universe — including all known compact-object + dark-energy + dark-matter probes via standardizable transients.
